overview: Individually randomised trial of group medical visits against usual individual reviews for adults with type 2 diabetes above target, across the practice and neighbouring practices, with partial nesting of groups in the intervention arm.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and HbA1c of 58 mmol/mol or more in the last six months, able to consent; excluded are people receiving palliative care or already in a structured education programme.
exposure: Intervention: six 90-minute group visits over 12 months for 8 to 12 patients, led by a practice nurse with a GP for part of each session, including short individual time. Comparator: usual individual reviews at the practice's usual frequency.
procedures: Eligible patients are identified from records and invited by letter; consenting patients are randomised 1:1 by a remote web system, stratified by practice and baseline HbA1c. Where possible, different nurses deliver group and individual care. HbA1c is measured at baseline and 12 months in routine blood tests; questionnaires are completed at baseline and 12 months.

outcomes.name: HbA1c at 12 months
outcomes.measure: HbA1c in mmol/mol from routine laboratory results
outcomes.why: The outcome trials report and the partners care about.

outcomes.name: Diabetes distress
outcomes.why: A patient-reported outcome the evidence rarely measures.

outcomes.name: Attendance
outcomes.measure: Proportion attending at least four of six group sessions
outcomes.why: Shows whether the offer reaches patients.

feasibility: About 580 patients are needed; the practice's own number is unknown, so neighbouring practices must join. Clinic time is within existing reviews.
biasMitigation: Remote randomisation stratified by practice and baseline HbA1c
Different nurses for the two arms where possible
Laboratory HbA1c as an objective primary outcome

biasFlags.label: Contamination through shared clinicians
biasFlags.note: Nurses delivering both formats may change usual care.

biasFlags.label: Unblinded questionnaires
biasFlags.note: Distress is self-reported by patients who know their allocation.

parsimony.simplestPath: One randomised comparison, one primary outcome, two stratification variables.

theoreticalFramework: None; the trial tests effectiveness of an established format.
summary: Partially nested individually randomised trial with HbA1c as the primary outcome.
